Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed today by learned counsel for the appellant is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 09.10.2023 passed by learned Special Judge (S.C./S.T. Act), Azamgarh in Bail Application No. 1004336 of 2023 (C.N.R. No. UPAZ010091922023) arising out of Case Crime No.
205 of 2023, under Sections 376-D, 452 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)5 S.C./S.T. Act, Police Lala Rajbhar @ Aadarsh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105489488/
1 Station-Deedarganj, District-Azamgarh and release the appellant on bail.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that in this case there is allegation against the appellant to commit rape with the victim with other two accused persons, namely, Rajan Yadav and Putiya Rajbhar.

On the same day the victim was taken to the hospital and medical aid was given,
but no injury either external or internal was found on the person of the victim to show that gang rape was committed with her by three persons including the appellant.

It is further submitted that the incident is said to have taken place in the house where other family members of the victim were also present and in such condition gang rape cannot be said to be possible in the night by gagging her mouth with cloth.

It is also submitted that in village rivalry the appellant is named in the F.I.R.
with other two co-accused persons.

It is next submitted that co-accused Putiya Rajbhar has already been granted bail by this Court in Criminal Appeal No. 10595 of 2023 vide order dated 08.02.2024 and the case of the present appellant is on similar footing.
The appellant is in jail since 11.08.2023 having no any criminal antecedent.
All these facts were not taken into consideration by the learned Special Judge while rejecting the bail, therefore, request to set it aside and allow the appeal.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid, but could not dispute the fact that co-accused Putiya Rajbhar has already been granted bail by this Court.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, medical report of the victim as well as the fact that co-accused has already been granted bail by this Court and the case of the present appellant is on similar footing, the Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant Lala Rajbhar @ Aadarsh involved in Case Crime No. 205 of 2023, under Sections 376-D, 452 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)5 S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Deedarganj, District-Azamgarh be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

sentences.text: 2 4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
